gpt.text:
Run the three commands in order; they’re designed to (1) search module variants and promote the best, (2) run system-level candidate sweeps, then (3) generate a concrete “next fix” plan from failures/regressions.

## 1) Module autopilot: select & promote best candidate
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to expect:
- Uses `module_registry.yaml` to enumerate module-level candidates/patches.
- Runs the eval suite for each.
- `--select-best` should automatically promote the best performer (often by writing/updating a “latest” champion JSON and/or symlinks, depending on your tooling).

After it finishes, verify:
- Which artifact was promoted (look for logs referencing `champion_v5_latest.json` or a new champion file).
- The reported `tuning_mean/min` and `lockbox_mean/min` vs the current champion numbers you pasted.

## 2) System autopilot: system-level candidate sweep
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to expect:
- Reads `system_candidates.yaml` (end-to-end/system configurations).
- Produces a report comparing candidates; may or may not auto-promote depending on your config.

After it finishes, check:
- Any regressions vs champion (especially `min`, since that often catches worst-case failures).
- Whether any candidates become “PASS” or “INCONCLUSIVE” and where they’re recorded.

## 3) Next-fix generator: actionable remediation list
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What to expect:
- Writes `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` summarizing the next most valuable fixes (typically driven by failing tests, worst-case samples, or regression clusters).

## Practical checks (so you don’t lose time)
- Run from repo root (so relative paths resolve).
- If your runs are long, capture logs:
  ```bash
  python3 ... 2>&1 | tee baseline/reports/run_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log
  ```
- After step (1), confirm whether the “current champion” file changed (timestamp/git diff).

## If you paste back results
If you paste the tail of each command’s output (promotion decision + metrics table), I can tell you:
- whether the new champion is truly better (mean vs min tradeoff),
- whether anything is “overfitting” tuning vs lockbox,
- and what the `next_fix.md` is implicitly prioritizing (and if that makes sense).
